structured_output.analysis: The best recipe, iso_3.15, has an average of 3.147953869 bits. The budget is 403/128 = 3.1484375 bits, so there are almost no spare bits. Most of the loss sits in MLP layers that use int3 or int2, and the measured int4 alternatives cut their single-layer KL by about 0.0035 to 0.0045 each. Moving a layer up one bit level costs about 1 bit per weight, so it has to be paid for somewhere. I fund those upgrades by setting group_size=256 for rht_gptq_int3, which roughly halves its per-group overhead across its 109 layers. I also try act_order=true, which costs no extra bits. Last round's proposals were refused only because they quoted an unsupported recipe-KL number, so these rationales quote only single-layer values from the cited records.

proposals.name: act_order_all_gptq
proposals.rationale: Same bits as the base. The worst layers are GPTQ int3/int2 MLP projections with heavy-tailed activations: model.layers.27.mlp.up_proj gptq_int3 has single-layer KL 0.0057182 [Ef04d8aa7bded] and activation kurtosis 1090.09 [E24beed188b6a]. Setting act_order=true, which quantizes columns in order of activation importance, should reduce error on outlier channels.

proposals.name: g256_rht3_fund_mlp_upgrades
